dominant_cause.pinned_mechanism: Diagnostic background loop CPU starvation and process/audit storm under QEMU emulation. In T663, t636-diag.sh ran multiple unthrottled background loops that continuously spawned subprocesses (toybox basename, tr, cat, pidof, mountpoint, mount, getprop). Specifically: (1) watch_zygote_environ iterated over all /proc/[0-9]* entries every 1 second, invoking toybox basename and tr for every process; when reading /proc/*/cmdline of non-toolbox daemons (vold, hal_*, etc.), it triggered SELinux denials (avc: denied { read/open } for comm='toybox') causing audit backlog overflow (audit_lost=51) and flooding the PL011 serial console via logcat; (2) watch_system_server polled every 200ms spawning getprop and toybox pidof; (3) watch_mirrors executed mountpoint -q every 500ms on tmpfs directories (/data/user_de/0, /data_mirror/...), which always fails in toybox because st_dev of a tmpfs child matches its tmpfs parent, causing it to execute mount -o bind repeatedly. Under QEMU TCG emulation, this continuous fork/exec storm and audit logging consumed all available CPU slices. When system_server reached Installer.connect() -> invalidateMounts() -> IInstalld.invalidateMounts(), installd (PID 2427) was starved of CPU while reading /proc/mounts and unable to return the Binder transaction. After 96 seconds of blockage, Watchdog killed system_server (PID 7917) at raw line 13498/14450.

candidate_a_diag_loop_cpu_starvation.evidence: In T663 flight-01, during the 96s block: 978 audit lines were emitted (10.2/s), 624 PIDs were created in 141s (4.4/s), audit buffer overflowed (audit_lost=51). ProcessCpuTracker in system_server failed with ENOENT trying to stat short-lived toybox PIDs (8543, 8553, 8556, 8559). SysRq CPU0 backtrace at line 13460 showed installd actively executing seq_read -> show_vfsmnt -> __d_path -> prepend_path, proving it was not deadlocked but starved of execution time under the process storm.

candidate_b_installd_invalidatemounts_co.evidence: In T660, Installer.onStart() took exactly 69 ms (line 10522). In T661, Installer.onStart() took exactly 160 ms (line 10599). In both tracks, installd parsed the identical ~45 mount lines from /proc/mounts under mMountsLock. The inherent cost of invalidateMounts itself is <200 ms and cannot explain a 96-second delay.

candidate_c_qemu_emulation_slowness_inde.evidence: QEMU 11.1.2 running on the exact same host hardware under identical emulation flags completed Installer.onStart() in 69 ms (T660) and 160 ms (T661). Pure emulation slowness without background loop contention adds negligible overhead (<100 ms).

dominant_cause.pinned_fix:
1. In watch_zygote_environ: exit immediately (return 0) once Zygote environment is marked (T642_ZYGOTE_ENVIRON_END); use shell parameter expansion ${proc##*/} instead of toybox basename; eliminate all background /proc scanning during system_server startup.
2. In watch_system_server: increase sleep interval from 0.2s to 2.0s, and check /proc/$active_ss_pid directly when alive instead of repeatedly invoking pidof.
3. In watch_mirrors: root mirror bind-mounts (/data/user_de/0, /data_mirror/...) are already established in do_prep() and must NOT be repeatedly mounted in a loop; increase package check sleep from 0.5s to 1.0s; retain in-memory seen_packages cache.
4. Preserve all T663 fixes intact: no pre-creation of dynamic UID packages (>10000), preserve CE/DE mirror mounts, 0 .capex.
